text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a 2h perf sweep on the continuous-batching change and extracted workload buckets. Seeing weird tail behavior when we mix very short prompts and long decode-rate sessions, esp on q4 kernels. Details below.

raj: thanks — short summary?

maria: TL;DR: batching buckets by prompt-length (<=64, 65-512, >512) + decode-rate buckets (fast/med/slow) helps kernel selection, but current queue policy creates starvation for slow-decode long contexts. p99 spikes ~2.3x.

oliver: can you paste the perf numbers and the config you used?

maria: perf snippet from perf-run-76: 
```
model: redwood-v2-13b
hw: a100-80g
workload-mix: 42% <=64, 38% 65-512, 20% >512
decode-rate-buckets: fast>50tps, med 10-50tps, slow<10tps
baseline p50/p95/p99: 8ms / 42ms / 120ms
post-change p50/p95/p99: 7.5ms / 48ms / 276ms
kv-cache hit-rate overall: 87% (but 55% for >512 slow decoders)
note: q4 kernel path shows GC stalls in profiler on >512 slow
```

raj: hmm 276ms p99 is bad. Where's the bottleneck — kernel selection or batching algorithm?

maria: profiler points to CPU-side queue churn and some SGEMM fallback on q4 for long sequences. Also KV cache serialization cost when multiple batches try to share the same cache entry (contention).

oliver: suggestion: change queue policy to priority by token-budget-per-batch, not purely FIFO. Give long-context slow-decode requests a smaller per-batch token budget so they don't force big kernels. Example config I tested: 
```
{
  "batching": {
    "buckets": [
      {"max_prompt_tokens": 64, "max_decode_rate": 9999, "target_batch_tokens": 2048},
      {"min_prompt_tokens": 65, "max_prompt_tokens": 512, "target_batch_tokens": 4096},
      {"min_prompt_tokens": 513, "target_batch_tokens": 1024, "adaptive": true}
    ],
    "queue_policy": "priority_by_token_budget",
    "token_budget_granularity": 64
  }
}
```

samantha: adaptive true for >512 — what does that mean?

oliver: adaptive -> reduce target_batch_tokens if decode-rate < 10tps; the goal is to avoid large joint batches that force q4 kernel. Instead let multiple small micro-batches go through faster kernels.

maria: I also tried a hybrid: allow small FIFO windows for short prompts (<=64) so you still get high batching efficiency, while prioritizing older long-context requests by token budget. That lowered p99 to ~160ms in the 30-min A/B run.

raj: nice. Any perf regression on throughput?

maria: throughput per-GPU dropped ~6% on mixed workload (because we trade some batching efficiency), but client-side tail improved hugely for long contexts. For Dedicated customers wanting predictable latency, it's better.

perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: https://perf.redwood.internal/fg/76 (shows CPU spin in queue manager and q4 fallback hotspots) :bar_chart:

oliver: other knobs: KV cache sharding (per-worker vs per-batch) — we saw contention when cache flush/serialize locked the batch thread. If we keep per-worker read-only view and apply diffs, GC stalls disappear.

maria: agreed. Next steps: (1) implement priority_by_token_budget in staging, (2) add adaptive token budget rules for decode-rate <10tps, (3) add KV cache per-worker snapshots to avoid serialization locks, (4) run 4h smoke with real traffic mix.

samantha: can I own the smoke test orchestration? I can set up canary with 10% of traffic on staging.

maria: please — assign to samantha. Also need a quick explainer for support: short doc on how buckets map to customer config and tradeoffs.

raj: minor: let's also add a metric for "effective batch token utilization" so we can track efficiency loss when adaptive kicks in.

maria: will add metric. One more note: kernel-selection table needs an override to prefer fp16/fast-gemm on short batches even if model nominally prefers q4 for cost. That flip saved ~18% p99 in trial.

oliver: good call. please include in PR description the perf-run id and diff commands: 
```
git diff -- perf/continuous_batching.go
python tools/eval_batching.py --workload-file workloads/mixed.json --dump-stats
```

maria: I'll open the PR after the staging smoke (ETA tomorrow). Thanks all. :thumbsup:

samantha: on it.

perf-bot: regression alert suppressed (manual triage) — reason: intended tradeoff.

maria: closing note: if anyone wants the raw traces I dumped (kv traces + per-kernel latencies), ping and I'll share a pre-signed link.
